newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson says U.S. court dismisses lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson says U.S. court dismisses lawsuit.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group Ericsson said on Wednesday that a U.S. district court had dismissed a lawsuit filed against it in December 1996 by Qualcomm Inc.

The company said it had also filed with the Southern District Court of California to seek dismissal of a second lawsuit bought by Qualcomm in February 1997 over alleged infringement of Qualcomm patents for narrowband CDMA handsets.

Ericsson said in the now-dismissed suit, Qualcomm charged Ericsson with unfair competition and impeding the acceptance and commercial deployment of Qualcomm's Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) technology and products.
The suit also sought a judicial declaration that certain Ericsson owned CDMA patents were not infringed upon by Qualcom.

Ericsson said it expects its own patent infringement suit against Qualcomm to proceed expeditiously now that the Federal District Court in Marshall, Texas had been confirmed as the venue for the case.
Ericsson said its case, filed in September 1996, alleged Qualcomm infringed numerous Ericsson patents pertaining to CDMA technology.
The company said the second lawsuit filed by Qualcomm was "frivolous".
Anders Torstensson, Ericsson cellular phones' general manager, said his company did not even make the handsets alleged in the lawsuit and has not offered to sell such handsets.
